PASSAGE V
Zadar’s Sea Organ
As I step off the ferry onto the Riva promenade in
Zadar, Croatia, I spot them—seven sets of long concrete
steps that descend into the sea. Stretching for over two
hundred feet along the curve of the coast, the steps are
awash with people strolling or sunbathing, waiting for
sunset. With gentle waves breaking against the lower
steps, the cordial, serene mood envelops me.
The scene is lovely, but I’ve seen lovely places
before. Below the murmuring voices and lapping water,
the haunting tones of Zadar’s Sea Organ resonate in my
chest like whale song. Despite years studying this
instrument’s design, I’m still surprised by what I hear in
person. The music is nothing like the bright, resounding
chords that fill cathedrals. These chords are slightly atonal,
actually, and unexpectedly soothing. Today, there’s also a
natural rhythm to the music—much like the rocking of a
boat, with the lower and higher notes—alternating in
volume as if on a sonic seesaw.
C
Hidden below the steps are thirty-five organ-like
pipes of various lengths. When waves meet the shore, they
propel air through the pipes and out vertical slots in the top
steps, generating a spectral array of sounds.
The writer wants to suggest that the people on the steps
aren’t too close together. Which choice best
accomplishes that goal?
A. No Change
B.
thronged
C.
sprinkled
D.
teeming
Which choice most effectively introduces the main
focus of the paragraph?
F. No Change
G.
lovely, and the sun glinting off the ocean enchants
me.
H.
lovely; I can’t wait to see more of this amazing
city.
J.
lovely, but I haven’t come to look; I’m here to
listen.
Which choice is clearest and most logical in context?
A. No Change
B.
Given how many years I’ve studied
C.
In the years I’ve spent studying
D.
Due to years of studying
Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically
acceptable?
F. No Change
G.
boat—with the lower and higher notes
H.
boat—with the lower and higher notes,
J.
boat with the lower and higher notes—
Which of the following accurate statements, if added
here, would most effectively introduce the paragraph?
A.
The Sea Organ has been “singing” since 2005.
B.
The pipes make intriguingly dissonant sounds.
C.
The Sea Organ is “played” by waves.
D.
The design has won several awards.
